title: Higher direct images along limits of cartesian squares
statement:
Let $I$ be directed and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X_i&\xleftarrow{\;h_i\;}&Y_i\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f_i}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e_i}\\
S_i&\xleftarrow{\;g_i\;}&T_i
\end{array}
\qquad(i\in I)
$$

be an inverse system of
cartesian squares with affine
transition morphisms, where every $g_i$ is
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$, $Y=\varprojlim_iY_i$, $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ and $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$; their induced limit square is

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
S&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$

Write $p_i:T\to T_i$ for the projections. All sheaves are on the small etale sites. If $(F_i)$ is a compatible system of torsion abelian sheaves on
$T_i$ (with transition morphisms $a_{ji}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws for the transitions $a_{ji}:T_j\to T_i$), $F=\varinjlim_ip_i^{-1}F_i$, and if for a fixed $q\ge0$ every
base-change map

$$
f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}F_i\longrightarrow R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i
$$

is an isomorphism, then so is

$$
f^{-1}R^qg_*F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F.
$$

(*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag `0EZT`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZT), second
assertion; the first assertion of that tag, for sheaves of sets, is not used
in this chapter.) In the Stacks Project this assertion is deduced from Lemma 59.51.8,
[Tag `0EYM`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYM)
(higher direct images commute with filtered colimits along an inverse
system whose transition morphisms are affine), applied to the two sides
of the base-change map.
The torsion hypothesis recorded here is the case used in this chapter, whose
coefficients are $\kunZn$-module sheaves.

proof.text:
Write $r_i:X\to X_i$, $s_i:S\to S_i$, $p_i:T\to T_i$ and $t_i:Y\to Y_i$ for the projections. The limit square is cartesian directly from the universal properties: maps $Z\to X$ and $Z\to T$ with equal composites to $S$ give, at every stage, a unique map $Z\to Y_i$; these maps are compatible because their two projections are compatible and the stage square has the pullback uniqueness property. They therefore give a unique map $Z\to Y$ with the prescribed projections. Because the stage squares are cartesian, $h_i$ is a base change of $g_i$ and hence is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Apply the sheaf-level composition identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition](1) to $p_i e=e_i t_i$. Since inverse image preserves colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], the coprojections give
$$e^{-1}F\cong\varinjlim_i e^{-1}p_i^{-1}F_i\cong\varinjlim_i t_i^{-1}e_i^{-1}F_i.$$
The transition from $i$ to $j$ on the latter system is inverse image of the given coefficient transition, conjugated by these composition identifications. Their associativity gives the identity and composition laws, so this is a system to which relative continuity applies.

source.place: Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, proof: qcqs base change and the coefficient colimit on Y

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-0eym] to the inverse system $g_i:T_i\to S_i$ and the given coefficient system. Both its source and base transition morphisms are affine by hypothesis, and every $g_i$ is qcqs. Its canonical comparison gives $R^qg_*F\cong\varinjlim_i s_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}F_i$. Pull back along $f$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], followed by the composition identifications for $s_i f=f_i r_i$ from [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], to obtain the canonical isomorphism
$$C_A:\varinjlim_i A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}R^qg_*F,\qquad A_i=r_i^{-1}f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}F_i.$$
The legs of $C_A$ are the inverse images of the specified continuity legs, with precisely those composition identifications.

source.place: Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, proof: the second displayed continuity equality, for the source

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-0eym] to $h_i:Y_i\to X_i$ and the coefficient system $e_i^{-1}F_i$ of Step 1. The four given systems supply affine transitions on $Y_i$ and $X_i$; the required qcqs hypotheses were checked in Step 1. Its limit coefficient is $e^{-1}F$, by that step. Thus its canonical legs give
$$C_B:\varinjlim_i B_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qh_*e^{-1}F,\qquad B_i=r_i^{-1}R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i.$$
No statement about the stages being cartesian over each other has been used.

source.place: Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, proof: the first displayed continuity equality, for the target

proof.text:
Let $\beta_i:f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}F_i\to R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i$ and $\beta:f^{-1}R^qg_*F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ be the specified exchange maps, and put $d_i=r_i^{-1}\beta_i:A_i\to B_i$. Write $x_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$, $y_{ji}:Y_j\to Y_i$, $a_{ji}:T_j\to T_i$ and $s_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$ for the four transition maps, and $\phi_{ji}:a_{ji}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ for the given coefficient map. We verify that the $d_i$ commute with transitions and with the limit legs.

First work on bounded below derived categories. Denote stage exchange by $E_i$, limit exchange by $E$, exchange for the square $(a_{ji},s_{ji},g_j,g_i)$ by $P_{ji}$, and exchange for $(y_{ji},x_{ji},h_j,h_i)$ by $Q_{ji}$. For these possibly noncartesian squares, use the mate formula displayed in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]: the square isomorphism is formed from the composition isomorphisms and the equality of composite morphisms. That formula involves no pullback universal property. For $K\in\Dplus((T_i)_{\Et})$, pasting along the nonadjoint sides by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) gives
$$
 E_j(a_{ji}^{-1}K)\circ f_j^{-1}P_{ji}(K)
 =Q_{ji}(e_i^{-1}K)\circ x_{ji}^{-1}E_i(K).
$$
Indeed both pasted square transformations start at $h_j^{-1}f_j^{-1}s_{ji}^{-1}$, identified with $h_j^{-1}x_{ji}^{-1}f_i^{-1}$, and end at $e_j^{-1}a_{ji}^{-1}g_i^{-1}$, identified with $y_{ji}^{-1}e_i^{-1}g_i^{-1}$. Both are the composition comparison through the common morphism $Y_j\to S_i$; their equality is exactly the associativity of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition](3). The mate formula therefore gives the displayed equality. Set $K=F_i[0]$ and postcompose with $Rh_{j,*}e_j^{-1}(\phi_{ji}[0])$. Naturality of $E_j$ in its coefficient, stated in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], moves this coefficient map past $E_j$. Pulling back by $r_j^{-1}$ and identifying $r_i=x_{ji}r_j$ gives the two diagram transition composites.

For the limit legs, define $P_i:s_i^{-1}Rg_{i,*}\to Rg_*p_i^{-1}$ and $Q_i:r_i^{-1}Rh_{i,*}\to Rh_*t_i^{-1}$ by the mate formula for the projection squares. Pasting gives the explicit equality
$$
 E(p_i^{-1}K)\circ f^{-1}P_i(K)
 =Q_i(e_i^{-1}K)\circ r_i^{-1}E_i(K).
$$
Here the two underlying square transformations run from $h^{-1}f^{-1}s_i^{-1}$ to $e^{-1}p_i^{-1}g_i^{-1}$ and are both the composition comparison through $Y\to S_i$, by the same cited associativity identity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) to these two transformations. Set $K=F_i[0]$ and postcompose with $Rh_*e^{-1}(\iota_i[0])$, where $\iota_i:p_i^{-1}F_i\to F$ is the coprojection. Naturality of $E$ moves this coefficient map to the source-side leg. Step 1 identifies $e^{-1}\iota_i$ with the coefficient leg used for $C_B$.

Take degree-$q$ cohomology in both equations. The natural cohomology identifications for exact inverse images follow from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. On the cartesian stage and limit squares, [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] identifies these maps with $\beta_i$ and $\beta$. On transition and projection squares they are the specified degree-$q$ mates in [lem-kun-0eym]. Thus, if $u_{ji}:A_i\to A_j$ and $v_{ji}:B_i\to B_j$ are the diagram transitions, the first equation gives $d_j u_{ji}=v_{ji}d_i$. If $\lambda_i:A_i\to f^{-1}R^qg_*F$ and $\mu_i:B_i\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ are the continuity legs, the second equation gives $\beta\lambda_i=\mu_i d_i$.

source.place: Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, final inference; explicit canonical-map check using the transition/leg construction of Tag 0EYM

proof.text: Every $\beta_i$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis, and a functor preserves its inverse, so every $d_i$ is an isomorphism. If $a_{ji}:A_i\to A_j$ and $b_{ji}:B_i\to B_j$ now denote the diagram transitions, Step 4 gives $d_j a_{ji}=b_{ji}d_i$, hence $a_{ji}d_i^{-1}=d_j^{-1}b_{ji}$. Thus the inverses also form a morphism of diagrams. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] induces mutually inverse morphisms $d:\varinjlim A_i\to\varinjlim B_i$ and $d^{-1}$, since their composites are the identity on every coprojection. The leg equation in Step 4 and the same uniqueness clause give $\beta C_A=C_B d$. Steps 2 and 3 identify $C_A,C_B$ as isomorphisms. Therefore $\beta=C_B d C_A^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, as required.

split_report.summary: Expanded Tag 0EZT into five steps, with separate source and target applications of varying-base continuity, a canonical-map cube verification using general mates, and an explicit inverse on the colimit. Added one unsplit continuity lemma, Tag 0EYM, after checking the whole DAG and blueprint: existing 09Z1 is fixed-base, and the cartesian higher-image nodes fix a sheaf and, in the continuity assertions, a field base. Clarified only the implicit limits, projections and small-etale topology in the statement; retained its torsion hypothesis and conclusion. No finished project declaration or Mathlib match found. Second reader supplied the universal-property proof that the limit square is cartesian and explicit derived stage/limit mate equations, including coefficient postcomposition and the exact-inverse-image cohomology identifications.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the entire sole blueprint proof paragraph: its two applications of Tag 0EYM and the final passage of stage base-change isomorphisms to the limit.

tool_uses.why: Generic abelian-sheaf inverse-image continuity needed on both sides of the prescribed 0EYM route; the unit has no replacement.
Canonical inverse-image composition and coherence identify coefficient systems and the cube maps; generic formal tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
General pasting formula for adjunction mates verifies compatibility of the canonical continuity and base-change maps, including noncartesian transition faces.
The canonical mate formula and coefficient naturality specify which base-change map is being compared.

Exactness of inverse image identifies the degree-q cohomology of the derived transition and leg equations with their sheaf-level formulas; a generic sheaf tool, leaving the prescribed continuity route unchanged.
